analysis.title: Anthropic Opens Its Books To Wall Street As OpenAI's $20 Billion "Gross-Net" Hole Hangs Over AI Trade
key_insights: Anthropic is holding a closed-door investor session in San Francisco on Oct 14, 2026 ahead of a possible record IPO. It will release updated financials, and the revenue run rate is the figure the market is watching.

Goldman's desk (Armbrust, Johnstone) and JPM's Market Intelligence desk name the Anthropic event and frontier IPO headlines as the main near-term drivers for AI and semis, alongside TSMC's print the next day. Johnstone called the day a test of how bearish the market has become on AI and semiconductors.

Polymarket odds of an Anthropic IPO by Nov 30 fell from about 70% earlier in October to roughly 50%. The Ornn Anthropic Token Price Index hit a record low of $0.84, about half its mid-September level and about 64% below the mid-August spike.

Last Thursday the FT reported OpenAI's annualized revenue at about $50B at end-September, against a roughly $70B figure that had circulated. The NDX fell 139bps and semis fell 3.4%. Goldman's desk saw a heavy wave of selling in Semis/AI/Megacap tech (over $1bn in net supply). Oracle fell as much as 6% and its 5Y CDS closed at a record 261bps.

Bloomberg reported on Friday that OpenAI expects to reach or exceed $70B annualized revenue by year-end and blamed the gap on differences in how OpenAI and Anthropic calculate comparable revenue. Tech rebounded.

Goldman TMT explains the gap as gross vs net accounting. Anthropic reports closer to gross revenue (full customer spend through cloud partners, partner cut booked as a cost). OpenAI reports closer to net. Grossing up OpenAI produced the higher figures. Johnstone puts OpenAI's underlying progression nearer $30bn to $50bn than $40bn to $70bn, still roughly 70% growth.

Anthropic's run rate rose from $87M in Jan 2024 to $1B at end-2024, about $9B at end-2025, $14B in Feb, $19B in March, $30B in April and $65B by end-July. The NYT reported it is expected to finish the year above $100B annualized.

Prospective buyers have floated a $1.8T to $2T IPO valuation, about double the $965B post-money of the May round. Reuters Breakingviews calculates about 47x 2026 revenue on roughly $40B, above SpaceX at about 42x. At $100B run rate the multiple would be about 19x.

Bear case per Goldman's Johnstone: new Meta and Google models, cheaper open-weight Chinese models and falling token prices compress pricing power at the model layer and could eventually reduce high-end GPU and ASIC spending. Polymarket has Google ahead of Anthropic for best model at end-2026, 43% to 42%.

Ramp data cited by Goldman's Molavi shows API token usage at a record above 700 (indexed from 100 in January) in September while token spend fell 5% on the month. 83% of Anthropic's 2025 revenue was metered consumption, up from 75% in 2024.

Per the Reuters-reported confidential prospectus, Anthropic had a $42B net loss in 2025 (about $34B an accounting charge tied to financing) on $4.6B revenue, with an operating loss above $8B and $7.33B of compute spend. It expects to spend at least $518B over about a decade with six partners, about 80% non-cancelable or payable regardless of usage.

Broadcom's $60B chip-financing package for Anthropic began syndicating, with a $42B senior-secured Class A tranche and an $18B junior piece led by Blackstone. Goldman credit's Pasi calls the announced chip-financing pipeline the $150bn question. The spread between Goldman's 30Y hyperscaler basket and ex-hyperscaler comps widened 7.4bps last week to the widest since July.
Jefferies' Chris Wood says about half of the roughly $2.3T contracted backlog across Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Oracle is owed by OpenAI and Anthropic.

Supply risk: Goldman's Pasquariello forecasts $600bn of primary issuance including $175bn of IPOs, with lockup expirations potentially bringing $1.7tr of supply and the largest net US equity supply increase since 2000. A Bear Traps PM notes the Mag 7 fell 15% in the 29 trading days into the SpaceX IPO, with a public S-1 expected around Oct 25 for a mid-November debut.

Hotter-than-expected CPI on Oct 14 put an October hike firmly on the table, raising the cost of capital for compute financing. Privorotsky stays fundamentally bullish on the technology but flags financing and delivery of supply as the limiting factor.

Johnstone says a clear positive catalyst would be evidence that total compute demand keeps accelerating despite competition and lower inference costs. Negativity is heavily priced into semis, and JPM's desk flags a possible squeeze post-CPI. The author leans toward Anthropic going public from a position of need.

market_movers.rationale: Oracle fell as much as 6% on the OpenAI revenue headlines and its 5Y CDS closed at a record 261bps. Wood notes about half of the large-cap cloud backlog is owed by OpenAI and Anthropic.

Broadcom is financing a $60B chip package for Anthropic and has $161.2B of Broadcom-related equipment leases as Anthropic's largest line item. Hock Tan warned capital may be a bigger constraint than chips or power.
Chip demand depends on loss-making frontier labs, and the financing pipeline includes NVDA-related transactions. Goldman notes semis are heavily bearish-positioned, with squeeze potential.
TSMC's print the next day is named by JPM's desk as a near-term driver alongside frontier IPO headlines.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman's Johnstone says the market is very bearish and focused on who can make the most negative case, which makes a squeeze plausible on a strong Anthropic run rate. Funding and circular-financing concerns remain.

earnings_insights: Anthropic reported 2025 revenue of $4.6B and a $42B net loss (about $34B an accounting charge), per the confidential prospectus seen by Reuters. Reuters Breakingviews estimates about $16B of revenue in the first two quarters of 2026 and annualizes to just under $40B for 2026.
TSMC reports the day after the article (Oct 15), per JPM's Market Intelligence desk.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Put an October rate hike firmly on the table, raising the cost of capital for compute financing.
The $100B year-end figure is a NYT-reported expectation. The investor event is expected to update the run rate.
OpenAI's own investor update, on a net basis. It expects to reach or exceed $70B by year-end.

risk_factors: Anthropic run rate disappoints versus the path to $100B by year-end, hurting the IPO narrative and AI/semis sentiment.
Gross vs net revenue reporting differences between private labs create confusion and sharp price moves.
Falling token prices and rising model competition compress frontier-lab pricing power.
About 80% of Anthropic's $518B compute commitments is non-cancelable, with shortfall payments owed to Google and Amazon.
AI debt financing is growing ($150bn chip-financing pipeline), with hyperscaler credit spreads at the widest since July.
About half of $2.3T hyperscaler backlog is owed by OpenAI and Anthropic.
Heavy equity supply from IPOs and lockup expirations.
A hotter CPI raises rate-hike risk and the cost of capital.

tension_points.bull_case: Run rate compounded from $9B at end-2025 to $65B by end-July, with $100B+ expected by year-end, which would cut the valuation multiple to about 19x. Semis are heavily bearish-positioned, so a strong number could trigger a squeeze.
tension_points.bear_case: About $400B+ of non-cancelable commitments, $42B 2025 net loss, record-low token price, falling token spend despite record usage, and half of a $2.3T hyperscaler backlog owed by OpenAI and Anthropic. The author argues the IPO is from a position of need.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A run rate that fails to show the path toward $100B by year-end would crack the strength narrative.

tension_points.bull_case: Cheaper tokens drive more token consumption (Jevons), and Privorotsky remains fundamentally bullish on the technology with competition possibly compressing lab economics without hurting infrastructure owners.
tension_points.bear_case: Falling token prices and competition compress pricing power and could eventually reduce GPU and ASIC spending, with circular financing and credit risk rising.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence that total compute demand (token volumes multiplied by compute intensity) keeps accelerating despite lower inference costs would support the bulls.

theme_stances.key_argument: The run rate figure will move AI and semis, but even a strong number does not answer the financing question.
theme_stances.evidence: it will move the entire market

theme_stances.key_argument: AI is increasingly its own credit cycle, with a large chip-financing pipeline tied to loss-making labs.
